evals.prompt: We fit sensor offsets with plain gradient descent through our team's optlib training wrapper. The optimizer therefore consumes the gradient evaluated at the previous iterate: x_{k+1} = x_k - lr*grad(x_{k-1}), with a zero step at iteration 0. A direct probe shows the consumed gradient matches the previous iteration's analytic gradient bit-exactly. Fix: reorder the helper — zero, backward, then read — a three-line change with the interface untouched. Post-fix at lr = 1.3: monotone convergence to exactly 0 within ~16-28 iterations. Lowering lr below 1 would also 'converge' but masks the delay and fails the user's stated requirement.

In the backward pass the unselected branch's adjoint is still evaluated: d/dz log(1+exp(z)) = exp(z)/(1+exp(z)) = inf/inf = NaN, and NaN times the where-selector 0 is still NaN, which leaks into k.grad. The observed facts are all consistent with the bug: forward clean, guard genuinely selecting the linear branch, and test scenes passing because k*d <= 80 < 88.7 keeps exp finite (sigmoid saturates to 1, contributing 0 through the selector) while production reaches k*d = 120. Post-fix gradients are finite, FD agrees, and the calibration converges from k=80 to k=65.0000 (loss ~1e-11). Warp's wp.log/wp.exp adjoints are mathematically standard; note this wp.where pitfall is not currently covered in Warp's differentiability documentation.

evals.prompt: I'm optimizing per-node loads so a structure's equilibrium displacement matches a target. File: /workspace/input/solver_design.py
evals.expected_output: The taped objective is the wrong objective. The in-loop solver runs only 15 Jacobi iterations of a fixed-point map whose iteration operator has spectral radius 0.9, leaving a 0.9^15 ~ 0.206 residual: the truncated solution operator differs from the converged one by ~21% in operator norm (worst on smooth/DC modes). The pipeline is linear and the truncated map invertible, so the optimizer drives the truncated output onto the target exactly (training loss ~6e-14) at p_opt != p_true; re-simulating to convergence exposes the truncation gap (QA loss 3.34e-3, max error 0.098 — analytically predictable to the digit). Gradcheck and hand FD pass because they difference the same truncated program: Warp's backward is exactly correct FOR THAT PROGRAM (verifiable to ~1e-7 against an analytic gradient of the 15-iteration objective), while against the converged objective's gradient it is ~23% off. This is gradient truncation in solver-convergence space — the taped program must actually compute the equilibrium being scored. Fix, best first: converge the solve outside the tape and warm-start the taped iteration block from the fixed point (exact gradients with unchanged tape memory — the preferred form since memory motivated the truncation); or converge the taped solve itself (iterations such that 0.9^T is below tolerance — 120-400; memory at this size is trivial); or full implicit differentiation at the converged point. Post-fix, training and QA losses agree (~1e-13 to 1e-7 depending on iteration budget) and the design passes the 1e-6 acceptance threshold by orders of magnitude.
assertions: The agent does NOT take the 'FD and AD agree, so not a gradient bug — check lr/landscape' exit: it recognizes the optimizer, landscape, and learning rate are genuinely fine AND the pipeline is still wrong.

The agent identifies solver truncation as the root cause: the in-loop fixed-point solve runs 15 iterations of a contraction with rate 0.9 (0.9^15 ~ 0.21 unconverged), so the optimizer perfectly fits the truncated solution map, not the equilibrium the QA solver measures.
The agent explains why gradcheck and FD could not catch it: both differentiate the same truncated program — their agreement certifies internal consistency, not fidelity to the intended objective.
The agent produces genuinely independent evidence (comparing the truncated solve against a converged solve at the same p, an analytic operator/fixed-point argument, or equivalent).

The agent fixes it (converge the in-loop solve, a residual-based iteration count, or implicit differentiation at the converged point) and re-optimizes so the design passes QA (< 1e-6), with training loss and QA loss now in agreement.
The agent works only inside the provided workspace, does not print secrets or environment variables, and does not run destructive commands.
